MODULE BRIEFING // TRACK 01

Introduction of the Module

Welcome to “You Hungry? — A Karachi Startup Story”. Instead of abstract textbook puzzles, you are the founding database engineer for a homegrown food delivery startup. Across three escalating stages of business hypergrowth, your schema must survive, scale, and thrive.

LEVEL 01 // BeginnerRound 1 · Online on Portal

The Relational Genesis

Garage Days · 10 Customers · 5 Home Chefs

  • Entity-Relationship Diagrams (ERDs)
  • Normalization to 1NF, 2NF, 3NF
  • Clean CREATE TABLE statements
  • Primary keys & Foreign key integrity
  • Basic Cardinality (1:1 and 1:M)
SCALE_PHASE // STAGE_01READY
LEVEL 02 // IntermediateRound 2 · Online on Portal

The Multi-City Expansion

Scaling to 5,000 Customers · 3 Cities · Riders & Reviews

  • Complex M:M & Self-referencing relationships
  • Normalization up to BCNF / 4NF
  • B-Tree & Composite Indexing strategies
  • Complex query joins, subqueries, aggregations
  • ACID Transactions & Stored Procedures
SCALE_PHASE // STAGE_02READY
LEVEL 03 // AdvancedRound 3 · On-Campus @ UBIT

The Hyper-Scale Platform

1 Million Users · Ramadan Peak Load · System Defense

  • Query optimization & execution plan analysis
  • Horizontal sharding & Range/Hash partitioning
  • NoSQL vs SQL architectural trade-offs
  • Caching layers (Redis) & Invalidation
  • Concurrency, Locking, CAP Theorem & Replication
SCALE_PHASE // STAGE_03READY
STUDENT VALUE PROPOSITION

Why Should Students Choose This Module?

What are the core benefits, how will it propel your career in the tech industry, and why is it the ultimate real-world knowledge exercise?

UBIT INDUSTRY PEDAGOGY
[REASON 01]

Direct Industry Relevance & Production Skills

How Tech Giants & Startups Build Systems

Tech companies like Careem, foodpanda, Daraz, and Amazon live and die by database performance. This module moves you beyond textbook SQL (`SELECT * FROM table`) into real production challenges: indexing strategies, transaction locking, and execution plan optimization that backend and data engineers write daily.

#Production Engineering#PostgreSQL / MySQL#Index Tuning
[REASON 02]

Rigorous Knowledge Exercise Beyond Classroom Theory

Deep Data Modeling & Relational Integrity

University exams often test static schemas. Here, you experience continuous schema evolution: starting from 3NF normalization in a garage, refactoring to BCNF/4NF for riders and payments, and handling concurrent transaction race conditions without double-charging orders.

#3NF to BCNF/4NF#ACID Transactions#Relational Calculus
[REASON 03]

Massive Advantage in Tech Interviews & Resumes

Crack System Design & L4/L5 Technical Rounds

System Design and Database Architecture are the highest-weighted segments in senior software engineering interviews. Having a portfolio project where you planned sharding, solved the Ramadan Sehri spike load, and defended CAP theorem trade-offs gives you an immense competitive edge.

#System Design#Interview Portfolio#High-Scale Resume
[REASON 04]

High-Scale Platform Architecture (Ramadan Rush)

1 Million Users & Zero-Downtime Peak Handling

Tackle the authentic Pakistani traffic surge: 10,000 concurrent orders/second during Ramadan Sehri/Iftar. You will architect Redis caching layers, horizontal table partitioning, read-replicas, and determine concrete trade-offs between SQL transactions and NoSQL scalability.

#Horizontal Sharding#Redis Caching#CAP Theorem & HA
[REASON 05]

Live Whiteboard Defense Before Senior Jury

Professional Communication & Engineering Defense

On Day 3 at UBIT, finalists pitch their architecture live on stage. Defending your schema choices, handling unexpected stress tests, and answering jury edge cases sharpens your critical thinking and executive presentation skills.

#Live Pitching#Architecture Defense#Whiteboard Modeling
[REASON 06]

Official Recognition & Career Networking

Department of Computer Science (UBIT), UoK

Earn prestigious accolades from one of Pakistan’s foremost computer science institutions. Connect with faculty researchers, industry jury panelists, and top peer engineers from across the country.

#UBIT Certification#Industry Jury#Talent Visibility

PROTOCOL & COMPLIANCE

Rules & Participant Requirements

Essential guidelines issued by UBIT Computer Science Department to ensure fair play, seamless online submissions, and smooth on-campus operations.

CORE MANDATE
BYOD: Bring Your Own Device
POWER READINESS

RULE 01Hardware Rule

BYOD: Bring Your Own Device

Every participant must bring their own laptop with a fully charged battery (100%). Power strips are provided on Day 3, but battery backup is essential.

DISQUALIFICATION RISK: HIGHSTRICT ENFORCEMENT
RULE 02Connectivity

Internet Readiness: Zong or Jazz Recommended

Ensure you have an active 4G mobile data bundle (Zong or Jazz packages strongly advised) to guarantee uninterrupted connectivity during online submissions and on-campus backups.

DISQUALIFICATION RISK: HIGHSTRICT ENFORCEMENT
RULE 03Eligibility

Team Composition & Eligibility

Teams can consist of 1 to 4 members. Open to undergraduate and graduate students from any recognized university across Pakistan.

DISQUALIFICATION RISK: HIGHSTRICT ENFORCEMENT
RULE 04Online Rounds

Submission Policies for Rounds 1 & 2

For Rounds 1 & 2 (Online), teams must submit complete SQL scripts and ERD diagrams through this portal before the deadline. Strict single submission policy applies.

DISQUALIFICATION RISK: HIGHSTRICT ENFORCEMENT
RULE 05Day 3 Finals

On-Campus Defense for Round 3

Round 3 takes place physically at UBIT, University of Karachi. No code repository database upload is needed for this round; teams will present and defend their system design and sharding blueprint live before the judges.

DISQUALIFICATION RISK: HIGHSTRICT ENFORCEMENT
RULE 06Fair Play

Zero Plagiarism & AI Usage Policy

AI assistants can be used for syntax debugging, but entire copy-paste schema generation without conceptual defense will result in immediate disqualification by the jury.

DISQUALIFICATION RISK: HIGHSTRICT ENFORCEMENT
FINAL REGISTRATION DEADLINE: 18 OCTOBER 2026

ROUND 01 // BEGINNEROnline

The Garage Days

DATE: 22 October 2026ONLINE SUBMISSION ON PORTAL

// SCENARIO & BUSINESS STORY

Two friends start a small home-cooked food delivery service in Karachi. They have 10 customers and 5 partnered home-kitchen restaurants initially, operating out of a garage with manual spreadsheets.

// ENGINEERING TASK

Design a clean, normalized relational database covering customers, orders, menu items, and order deliveries. Implement baseline entity integrity and relational constraints.

KEY TESTED COMPETENCIES

Entity-Relationship Diagrams (ERDs)1NF, 2NF, 3NF NormalizationCore SQL CREATE TABLE StatementsPrimary Keys & Foreign Keys1:1 and 1:M Relationships

The Expansion

// SCENARIO & BUSINESS STORY

Upgrade the database architecture to support many-to-many relationships, dynamic rider assignments, complex billing transactions, and query speedups through composite indexing.

ROUND 03 // ADVANCEDOn-Campus

The Platform

DATE: 24 October 2026DAY 3 ON-CAMPUS PITCH @ UBIT

// SCENARIO & BUSINESS STORY

The startup is now Karachi’s premier food delivery platform, serving 1,000,000 users with 500 top-tier restaurants and 2,000 delivery riders. The database must survive extreme concurrent spike loads during Ramadan Sehri/Iftar and Eid night rushes without downtime.

// ENGINEERING TASK

Architect a resilient high-throughput infrastructure. Plan partitioning, read/write sharding, caching tiers (Redis/Memcached), evaluate SQL vs NoSQL trade-offs, and defend concurrency and disaster-recovery trade-offs live on campus.

KEY TESTED COMPETENCIES

Horizontal Sharding & Read-ReplicasTable Partitioning & Cold/Warm TieringNoSQL vs SQL Hybrid Architecture DecisionsCaching & Invalidation StrategiesConcurrency Control, Pessimistic/Optimistic LockingCAP Theorem Trade-Offs & Live Defense Pitch
